During the inspection, a black bear and a spider monkey, not authorized on the current license, were present on the
premises. An acquisition record indicated that the bear was obtained April 20, 2026, and the spider monkey, per a facility
representative, was obtained temporarily six days ago. The animals were housed next to the other regulated animals and
the facility's current license does not authorize the exhibition of a Group 6 nonhuman primate or bears. Failure to acquire
authorization for specific groups of animals does not ensure that the facility is knowledgeable and capable of maintaining
compliance with the care, husbandry, housing, and handling of these species. Licenses must specifically authorize the
use of brachiating species of non-human primates (Group 6) and bears, and a licensee must obtain a new license before
using any animal beyond those types or numbers of animals authorized under the existing license. The licensee must
obtain a new license authorizing the use of bears and spider monkeys for regulated purposes.
Corrections begun by applying for a new license at the time of inspection, and to remain corrected from this date forward,
August 19, 2026.

The facility did not maintain records which fully and correctly disclose information concerning certain animals in their
possession. The disposition of a Virginia opossum and the acquisition of a black-handed spider monkey were not
available at the time of inspection. Accurate records are required to identify legal ownership and to allow for tracing of
animals. Acquisition records of animals on hand shall include offspring born at the facility and shall include all required
information: name and address of person from whom animal was acquired, their USDA number or if unlicensed their
driver’s license and state and vehicle license number and state, date of acquisition/birth if born on property and species of
animal.
Corrections begun at the time of inspection and to remain corrected from this date forward, August 19, 2026.

A complete head-to-tail physical examination was not performed for each dog or dog hybrid every 12 months as required
by the Animal Welfare Act. Two adult dogs, Shaggy and Nova, a dog hybrid, have not had a full physical examination
since March 18, 2025, according to the attending veterinarian’s records. Routine physical examinations are important so
that a veterinarian can inform the licensee of health issues the dogs may be experiencing, can lead to more timely
diagnosis and treatment of issues, and allows APHIS inspectors to ensure adequate veterinary care is being provided to
the dogs. Correct by ensuring all dogs have a complete physical examination by the veterinarian at least every 12
months.
Corrected at the time of inspection by obtaining exams for both dogs, and to remain corrected from this day forward,
August 19, 2026.

Three ducks, housed outdoors, did not have an adequately sized pool or other aquatic area provided that allows each bird
to conduct normal waterfowl behaviors, such as swimming, submarining, and/or foraging. Instead, they have access to
one area for water (a black rectangular tub) that was approximately 30 inches long by about 18 inches wide and only
about 7 inches tall. Additionally, there was only about 5 inches of water provided within it which was not deep enough for
the ducks to swim or to submarine. Failure to provide a pool or other aquatic area of sufficient surface area and depth, for
all aquatic birds in the enclosure to be able to express natural behaviors, can lead to increased stress and a decline in
physical condition. Primary enclosures housing wading and/or aquatic birds must contain a pool or other aquatic area and
a dry area that allows easy ingress or egress of the pool or other aquatic area. Pools and other aquatic areas must be of
sufficient surface area and depth to allow each bird to make normal postural and social adjustments, such as immersion,
bathing, swimming and foraging.
Corrections begun at the time of inspection, and to remain corrected from this date forward, August 19, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
